narr: Thunderstorms developed late in the evening of July 22nd across northeast Illinois and continued into the morning of July 23rd. Numerous thunderstorms moved over the same areas across portions of Lake County, producing torrential rain and flash flooding. Large hail also occurred. Three tornadoes occurred in the southern suburbs of Chicago just after sunrise. Additional thunderstorms developed during the morning and continued into the afternoon of July 23rd, producing isolated large hail and wind damage.
ev: Numerous thunderstorms moved across Lake County during the early morning of July 23rd, producing torrential rain which led to flash flooding across east central portions of the county. Many roads were flooded and closed in Lake Bluff with several feet of water reported on some roads. Route 41 was closed between Route 137 and Route 176 where major flooding was reported. Several vehicles in Lake Bluff, Lake Forest and Highland Park got stuck in the flooding on roadways. Water rescues were performed along the North Shore. Basement flooding was reported in the Lake Bluff area. Interstate 94 was closed near Park Avenue due to flooding. Route 45 was closed at Casey Road due to flooding. The Deerfield High School track was flooded with a few feet of water. Storm total rainfall amounts included 6.68 inches in Lake Bluff; 6.60 inches in Zion; 5.74 inches in Libertyville; 5.54 inches in Lake Forest; 5.12 inches in Deerfield; 4.72 inches in Highwood; 4.34 inches in Mundelein; 4.32 inches in Vernon Hills and 4.26 inches at the Waukegan Airport.
